title: Grade 9 Mathematics — Quadrilaterals & Areas of Parallelograms
description: Quadrilaterals and Areas of Parallelograms and Triangles practice questions
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral is:
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral can be divided into two triangles, each with angle sum 180°. So total = 2 × 180° = 360°.

questions.question: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are:
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal (e.g., ∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠D). Adjacent angles are supplementary (add to 180°).

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus:
questions.explanation: In a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other at right angles (perpendicular bisectors). They may not be equal in length (that would make it a square).

questions.question: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. Then ∠B =
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, adjacent angles are supplementary: ∠A + ∠B = 180°. So ∠B = 180° − 70° = 110°.

questions.question: The midpoint theorem states that the line segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is:
options: Parallel to the third side and half its length
questions.explanation: The Midpoint Theorem: the segment connecting the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and exactly half its length.

questions.question: In a rectangle, the diagonals are:
options: Unequal and bisect each other at 90°
questions.explanation: In a rectangle, the diagonals are equal in length and bisect each other. (They are not perpendicular unless it is a square.)

questions.question: ABCD is a parallelogram with AB = 10 cm and BC = 6 cm. Its perimeter is:
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal: AB = CD = 10 cm and BC = DA = 6 cm. Perimeter = 2(AB + BC) = 2(10 + 6) = 32 cm.

questions.question: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 70°, 80°, and 110°. The fourth angle is:
questions.explanation: Sum of all angles = 360°. Fourth angle = 360° − 70° − 80° − 110° = 100°.

questions.question: Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallel lines have:
questions.explanation: This is an important theorem: parallelograms on the same base (or equal bases) between the same pair of parallel lines are equal in area.

questions.question: The area of a parallelogram with base 8 cm and height 5 cm is:
questions.explanation: Area of parallelogram = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

questions.question: A triangle and a parallelogram have the same base and are between the same parallels. The area of the triangle is:
questions.explanation: A triangle on the same base and between the same parallels as a parallelogram has half the area of that parallelogram.

questions.question: The area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 9 cm is:
questions.explanation: Area of triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 cm².

questions.question: The median of a triangle divides it into two triangles of:
questions.explanation: A median divides a triangle into two triangles with the same base length (two halves of the side bisected) and the same height. Hence, both have equal areas.

questions.question: If a parallelogram and a rectangle are on the same base and between the same parallels, then they have:
questions.explanation: Both have the same base and height (distance between parallels), so area = base × height for both. They have equal areas.

questions.question: In △ABC, D is the midpoint of BC. If the area of △ABC = 48 cm², then the area of △ABD =
questions.explanation: AD is the median of △ABC. The median divides a triangle into two equal areas. So area of △ABD = ½ × 48 = 24 cm².
